battle.name: 幫源洞之戰
battle.brief: 宣和三年（1121）十一月，北宋東路統制劉延慶自廣陽軍率眾直趨燕京，至燕京東北幫源洞遭遼將宗弼出城阻擊，宋軍先鋒大潰，器械輜重棄滿道塗。遼軍追抵城下，蕭綽與宗弼議定焚城遁去，童貫中路大軍至而見空城，遂奏「克燕」。此役為北宋聯金滅遼之戰開端，也是海上之盟反噬的伏筆。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 幫源洞之戰的交戰雙方，是北宋朝廷與契丹遼國的燕京留守軍。北伐由童貫以宣撫使總其事的京師禁軍，加上河北、山東、秦晉各路蕃漢兵為主力，另募河朔義軍與保甲壯丁；東路由統制劉延慶、副統制蔡靖率眾自廣陽軍北上，另有降將張覺以招撫使身分在前線效力，河北一帶的民兵則由宗澤整頓待用。命令自宣撫司下達，東、中兩路互不隸屬，前線將佐各徵本地轉運，糧秣由河北諸州沿運河轉輸至軍前。遼方並非全境勤王，留在燕京的是南京析津府的守軍與京畿諸州縣之兵，由蕭綽以太妃身分總攝軍國，契丹、漢人與蕃兵混編，樞密院與州縣的指揮系統合為一體，守城的還有燕京居民與各縣丁壯。燕京是遼五京之一，倉廩府庫與兵甲儲備俱足，地當幽雲孔道，北倚居庸，南望白溝，東出即密雲山區，正是遼廷倚為屏蔽的南面根本。蕭綽與將佐爭議的焦點，也在此刻成形：死守燕京以待援，還是棄城南撤，因為宋軍已壓到城下了。
countriesEn: The two sides in the battle of Aidingyuan were the court of the Northern Song and the garrison of Yanjing held by the Khitan Liao. The northern expedition was led, as commissioner for the expedition, by Tong Guan, and the main strength of the army was the imperial guards of the capital together with native and Chinese troops from the circuits of Hebei, Shandong, Qin and Jin, with volunteers from the lands north of the Yellow River and militia of the baojia enrolled besides them. The eastern route was under the command of Liu Yanqing, with Cai Jing as deputy, and they marched north from Guangyang army; the surrendered Liao general Zhang Jue served on the front line as commissioner for the pacification of Yanjing, and in the circuit of Hebei the local militia was being drilled by Zong Ze for use in the campaign. The orders came down from the expedition commission, and the eastern and central routes were not subordinate to one another: the officers on the front drew what they needed from the transport officers of their own localities, and grain and provisions reached the army by the water routes of the Hebei circuits. The Liao had not sent the whole realm to the rescue. What remained at Yanjing was the garrison of the southern capital of Xijing together with the troops of the prefectures and counties around the capital, under the authority of Empress Dowager Xiao, who as the senior consort directed the government of the state; Khitans, Han and native troops were mixed in the same units, and the privy council and the local commands were welded into a single chain of authority, with the residents of the city and the county militia manning the walls. Yanjing was one of the five capitals of the Liao; its granaries, its treasury and its armoury were all well stocked. It commanded the corridor of You and Yun, with Juyong to the north, the White Ditch to the south, and the mountains of Miyun to the east, and it was in fact the southern pillar of the Liao state. The question that divided the Empress Dowager and her commanders was settled at that moment: to hold Yanjing and wait for succour, or to leave the city and fall back, for the Song army was already at the walls.
people: 宋方主角是東路統制劉延慶。此人前鎮環慶，以調度有方著稱，也以貪墨軍資為御史所彈，北伐前正恃童貫之勢節制北軍；副統制蔡靖則是老成持重之輩，屢以持重為詞，兩人同軍而不同心，遇敵進退便生齟齬。降將張覺原為遼將，歸宋後任燕京招撫使，既熟悉幽燕山川，又不得志於同列，是日後生變的伏線。宣撫使童貫以宦官領兵，與副使蔡攸、宰相王黼同主和戰之議，萬一收復燕雲之功到手，封賞便隨之而至；河北一線的將佐如張所、姚平仲等亦在軍中效力。遼方，蕭綽是實際主政者，宗弼是本役的決定人物：他本姓張，漢人，早年效力於遼，在燕京軍中領兵多年，臨陣敢於出城野戰，又能服眾；遼主天祚帝耶律延禧此時已出奔在外，西行無歸，國事全憑蕭綽與宗弼一文一武撐持。宗弼後來降金，改姓完顏，成為金初年最著名的統帥之一，他在此役中大破宋軍的經歷，與後來金人南向時的用兵風格直接相關。事後與宋交涉、索取燕雲十六州的使臣，是馬伸與詹度。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Song side was the commander of the eastern route, Liu Yanqing. He had formerly governed Huanqing, was credited with orderly administration, and was also impeached for embezzling military funds; before the campaign he held the northern troops on the strength of Tong Guan's patronage. His deputy, Cai Jing, was an old and cautious hand who said again and again in favour of deliberation, and the two men served in one army without trust between them, so that every decision to advance or to withdraw at the first contact with the enemy produced friction. The surrendered general Zhang Jue had been a Liao officer; after coming over to the Song he was made commissioner for the pacification of Yanjing, and though he knew the mountains and waters of You and Yan intimately he was out of favour with his colleagues, and this was the fault line of the trouble to come. The commissioner for the expedition, Tong Guan, was a eunuch who led armies, and with the deputy commissioner Cai Yao and the chancellor Wang Fu he was among the men who debated war and peace at court; should the recovery of You and Yun be achieved, rewards would follow at once. Officers such as Zhang Suo and Yao Pingzhong were also employed on the Hebei front. On the Liao side the real power was Empress Dowager Xiao, and the decisive man of the battle was Zongbi. He was born Zhang, a Han Chinese man who had served the Liao for years and led troops in the army of Yanjing; in battle he dared to ride out of the city and fight in the open, and he could hold his men together. The Liao emperor Tianzuo, Yelü Yanxi, had already fled west and had no road back, so that the affairs of the state rested entirely on the Empress Dowager and on Zongbi, one for the civil and one for the war. Zongbi later surrendered to the Jin and took the surname Wanyan, and became one of the most famous commanders of the early Jin; the experience of breaking the Song army in this battle stands directly behind the way the Jin fought when it turned south. The envoys who afterwards negotiated with the Song and demanded the return of the sixteen prefectures were Ma Shen and Zhan Du.
kits: 本卡的兵器是希臘火——拜占庭帝國在七世紀配在銅管裡的燃燒劑，配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。它在燕京的戰場上並不曾出現：宣和三年十一次的燕原，沒有拜占庭的銅管噴射器，也沒有裝著希臘火的戰船；那一年真正燃燒的，是宋軍攜來的猛火油與火藥兵器，是遼軍在撤退前自己點起的那把大火。希臘火之所以配給這場戰爭，是因為它代表的是一條技術路線——以稠油、硫黃、硝為主藥，以投擲器或噴管送出的燃燒兵器，配方保密、器械簡陋，命中即起黏著之火，扑滅不易。同一條路線在東亞有另一副面孔：《武經總要》所載的猛火油以皮囊盛貯，燃之不易熄，擲於水面亦能浮燃；宋軍攻城另有火砲、霹靂箭與火箭，專燒城門、樓櫓與守軍聚集之處。遼軍的守城裝備則以床弩、欹竿弩、擲石之砲與拒馬、鹿角、鷹巢為主，燕京城牆高厚，馬面突出，護城河闊，冬十一月水面結冰，攻城者可踏冰而過，守方卻也可趁冰封之時閉塞缺口。攻城實際器械另有雲梯、搭天梯、填壕木排與擲石車，運輸用太平車、牛馬與舟船，糧秣由河北沿運河轉輸。真正的希臘火同年卻在別處開火：拜占庭皇帝約翰二世於1121年再入敘利亞，拔貝魯特、進逼阿勒頗，以火攻與圍城術對付塞爾柱人的城塞——那才是這件兵器真正出鞘的地方。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is Greek fire, the burning mixture of the Byzantine empire in the seventh century, served in a copper tube; the formula was the secret of the empire, and the formula and the ship went down together. It did not appear on the field at Yanjing: in the eleventh month of Xuanhe 3 there was no Byzantine copper tube at Yanjing and no war galley loaded with Greek fire. What really burned that year was the burning oil and the gunpowder weapons the Song army had brought with it, and the great fire the Liao set themselves as they withdrew. Greek fire is given to this war because it stands for a line of technology — a burning charge made chiefly of thick oil, sulphur and saltpetre, delivered by a thrower or a tube, with the formula kept secret and the apparatus crude, which took hold at once and clung to what it struck and could not easily be put out. The same line of technology wore a different face in East Asia. The burning oil recorded in the Wujing Zongyao was carried in bladders, it was hard to put out, and thrown on the surface of water it would float and burn. The Song siege train also had fire bombs, thunderbolt arrows and fire arrows, meant for the gates, the wooden towers and the places where the defenders crowded together. The Liao defence relied on crossbows of the bed and the leaning-pole types, on stone-throwing engines, and on caltrops, deer-horn fences and nest-like firing platforms. The walls of Yanjing were tall and thick with projecting bastions and a broad moat; in the eleventh month the water of the moat froze, so that the besiegers could cross on the ice, and the defenders could use the frozen season to seal the breaches. The actual siege equipment also included scaling ladders, tall hook-ladders, wooden rafts for filling the ditch and engines for throwing stones, while transport was done with great flat carts, oxen, horses and boats, and the grain came up from Hebei by the waterways. The true Greek fire was busy in another place in the same year: the Byzantine emperor John II re-entered Syria in 1121, took Beirut and pressed on toward Aleppo, meeting the Seljuk fortresses with fire and with the arts of the siege, and that was where this weapon truly came out of its sheath.
tactics: 宋軍的打法是典型的北宋北伐式攻堅：先以大軍壓境，切斷關外，孤立幽雲；再令東路自廣陽軍沿大道北上，連下涿州、良鄉諸城，一路直抵燕京城下，企圖以合圍之勢迫遼廷放棄中都。實際戰法在幫源洞一步失手。燕京東北多山，自涿、良至密雲一線多山谷隘口，遼將宗弼不待宋軍攻城，先以所部出城迎戰，據山梁谷口節節設阻，令宋軍先鋒逐段深入而後合圍殲滅；宋軍長於平原列陣而短於山谷攻守，前鋒一破，中軍立潰，兵器、輜重、旗鼓棄滿道塗，數十里內塞道。遼軍乘勝追抵燕京城下，圍城數日，卻在下一步上失算：蕭綽與宗弼議定焚城而遁，先掠府庫、驅趕丁壯出城，然後四面放火，自己乘夜由西山或北門撤出，把一座空城留給宋軍。童貫中路大軍抵達時望見的只是煙火與空郭，當即報捷，朝廷於是按克城論功行賞。攻城技術細節亦可見於宋人記載：壕塹以土石填塞，雲梯、搭天梯倚牆而上，砲石拋擲城頭，猛火油灌入缺口，士卒裹溼氈衝火而入。入城之後，宋軍拆取城樓木料以資漕運，幽燕之民由是怨之，這一怨恨在一年之後化為反亂。
tacticsEn: The Song plan was the classic Northern Song way of taking a fortress: first to press the frontier with a mass of troops, cut the country off from outside, and isolate You and Yun; then to send the eastern route north along the great road from Guangyang, carrying the prefectures of Zhu and Liang one after another and coming straight up to the walls of Yanjing, in the hope of surrounding the Liao capital and forcing it to abandon the seat of the dynasty. What failed was a single step at Aidingyuan. North-east of Yanjing the country is all hills, and the line from Zhu and Liang to Miyun runs through a chain of valleys and passes. Rather than wait to be besieged, the Liao commander Zongbi led his men out of the city to meet the Song, held the ridges and the mouths of the valleys in succession, let the Song vanguard march in by degrees and then closed and destroyed it. The Song army was at its best deploying in the open plain and at its worst in a valley fight; once the vanguard broke, the centre gave way at once, and arms, baggage, flags and drums lay along the road for tens of li, blocking the way. The Liao pursued the routed army up to the walls of Yanjing and lay around the city for several days, and then lost the next step of the business: the Empress Dowager and Zongbi agreed to burn the city and withdraw, first stripping the treasury and driving the inhabitants out, then setting fire on all sides and leaving by night through the western hills or the northern gate, so as to hand the Song an empty city. When Tong Guan's central army arrived it saw only smoke and a hollow shell of a town, reported a capture at once, and the court rewarded the commanders as for a city taken. The details of the siege technique survive in Song accounts: the ditch filled in with earth and stone, scaling ladders and tall hook-ladders set against the wall, stones hurled at the parapet, burning oil poured into the breaches, and men wrapped in wet felt charging through the fire. After entering the city the Song army pulled down the timber of the towers for use in their transport works, and the people of You and Yan resented it; that resentment turned into revolt within a year.
data: 可核對的數字有限，須分清宣稱與實數。時間：宣和三年（1121）冬，宋軍攻燕在十月至十一月之間，戰於幫源洞多繫於十一月。兵力：北宋號稱二十萬大軍，東路統制劉延慶所部人數諸記多作十五萬，中路童貫直趨燕京者亦稱十餘萬，皆是宣撫司宣傳之數，實際列陣當遠少於此；遼方留在燕京者為南京禁軍與京畿州縣兵，數萬之眾，契丹、漢人、蕃兵混編，宗弼出戰之部當為城中精兵，具體人數無從考見。距離：廣陽軍（今河北雄縣一帶）至燕京約一百二十餘里，良鄉至燕京西門不過數十里，一日可至；幫源洞在燕京東北，去城約一日行程。兵器尺度：宋軍弩以《武經總要》所載神臂弓最遠，矢所及三百四十步，攻城則靠雲梯、砲與火藥兵器。戰果：宋軍大潰，死傷無算，器械輜重棄於途；遼軍追至城下而終不能守城，遂焚之而去，燕京府庫、圖籍付之一炬。事後驗證：宋廷以「收燕」論功，童貫封廣陽郡王、拜太師，劉延慶、蔡靖等亦受賞；然宣和四年（1122）初，幽州漢軍以賞罰不公、拆城役繁為由反亂，燕京復失，童貫引兵南退，降將張覺為遼人所誅；同年遼燕京降於金，金人遂據燕雲，五年（1125）遼亡，七年（1127）靖康之難隨之而至。對照：1121年，拜占庭皇帝約翰二世再入敘利亞，拔貝魯特、進逼阿勒頗。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are few, and the claimed figures have to be separated from the real ones. In time: in the winter of Xuanhe 3 (1121) the Song armies were before Yanjing between the tenth and the eleventh months, and the fighting at Aidingyuan is generally dated to the eleventh month. In strength: the Song proclaimed a great army of two hundred thousand; the number under the eastern commander Liu Yanqing is given in most accounts as one hundred and fifty thousand, and the central force under Tong Guan, marching straight on Yanjing, is also put at more than a hundred thousand — all of these are the figures of the expedition's publicity, and the number actually drawn up in the field must have been far lower. On the Liao side, what remained at Yanjing was the guard of the southern capital together with the troops of the prefectures and counties round it, a force of several tens of thousands in which Khitans, Han and native soldiers were mixed; the troops Zongbi led out were the picked men of the city, and their exact number cannot be recovered. In distance: from Guangyang army, in the neighbourhood of today's Xiongxian in Hebei, to Yanjing is about a hundred and twenty li; from Liangxiang to the west gate of Yanjing is no more than a few tens of li, a single day's march; Aidingyuan lies north-east of the city, about a day's journey from it. In the scale of the arms: the longest reach of the Song crossbows was the divine arm bow recorded in the Wujing Zongyao, whose arrow carries three hundred and forty paces, while the taking of the walls depended on scaling ladders, engines and gunpowder weapons. In results: the Song army was utterly routed with losses beyond counting, arms and baggage lying along the road; the Liao pursued to the walls but could not hold the city, and so burned it and went away, and the treasury and the archives of Yanjing were destroyed in the fire. The checking afterwards: the court credited the recovery of Yanjing, made Tong Guan Prince of Guangyang and Grand Preceptor, and rewarded Liu Yanqing, Cai Jing and the rest; yet in the early months of Xuanhe 4 (1122) the Han troops of Youzhou rose in revolt, with the unfair distribution of rewards, the heavy labour of pulling down the walls and the exactions as their pretexts; Yanjing was lost again, Tong Guan withdrew south, and the surrendered general Zhang Jue was executed by the Liao. In that same year Yanjing surrendered to the Jin and the Jin held You and Yun; in 1125 the Liao perished, and in 1127 the disaster of Jingkang followed. For comparison: in 1121 the Byzantine emperor John II re-entered Syria, took Beirut and pressed toward Aleppo.
cause: 打起來的原因是燕雲十六州。幽雲十六州自後晉石敬瑭割與契丹，到宋初已有百年，漢人故老日夜以望復為念；宋與遼又立白溝之盟，兩國不得越界一步。而遼主天祚帝荒怠，蕭綽雖能，國用竭、將相爭，屬國渤海、遼東與西夏各懷異志，社稷已非舊時之固。宋徽宗用王黼、童貫、蔡攸一輩好功之臣，把收回燕雲視為天下一統的關鍵，遂密結金人，約以海上之盟：宋出錢糧、兵力和情報，金以鐵騎自北而下列陣，兩家夾攻，遼亡之後燕雲歸宋。宣和元年（1119）冬海上之盟立約，宣和二年（1120）金人果出兵北伐，天祚帝出奔，遼廷在燕京人心惶惶；童貫遣使索取燕雲十六州，遼使拒之，朝廷於是轉議用兵。宣和三年（1121）正月，宋以童貫、蔡攸為宣撫、副宣撫使，調京師禁軍及河北、山東、秦晉蕃漢兵，號二十萬，分東、中兩路北伐。於是才有廣陽道上那一路直趨燕京，和它在密雲山中幫源洞的那一場遭遇。
causeEn: The reason for the war was the sixteen prefectures of You and Yun. Since Shi Jingtang of Later Jin had ceded them to the Khitans, a century had passed by the beginning of the Song, and the Han old men of the realm had never ceased to talk of recovering them; and the Song and the Liao had set the White Ditch as a frontier across which neither might step. The Liao emperor Tianzuo was dissolute; the Empress Dowager Xiao was able, but the treasury was empty, the ministers quarrelled, the vassal states of Bohai, Liaodong and Western Xia each had their own thoughts, and the state was no longer the solid thing it had been. Emperor Huizong of Song took the men who loved great deeds — Wang Fu, Tong Guan, Cai Yao — and made the recovery of You and Yun the condition of a single order under heaven, and so he made his secret compact with the Jin: the Song would supply money, grain, soldiers and intelligence, the Jin would send their cavalry down from the north, the two would strike together, and when the Liao fell the prefectures would go to the Song. The pact of the sea was sealed in the winter of Xuanhe 1 (1119); in Xuanhe 2 (1120) the Jin did send their army north, and Tianzuo fled abroad, and the Liao court at Yanjing was in an uproar of nerves. Tong Guan sent envoys to demand the sixteen prefectures, the Liao envoys refused, and the court turned to war. In the first month of Xuanhe 3 (1121) the Song appointed Tong Guan commissioner for the expedition and Cai Yao his deputy, drew the guards of the capital together with native and Chinese troops from Hebei, Shandong, Qin and Jin, proclaimed two hundred thousand men, and marched in two routes, east and centre, to the north. Hence the column that went straight up the road from Guangyang on Yanjing, and hence the encounter in the mountains of Miyun at Aidingyuan.
impact: 此役的影響，是北宋「收復燕雲」這條路線的第一次破產。宋廷在童貫的奏報裡得了燕京，得了封賞，得了「與契丹為兄弟、故地歸宋」的說法；但真正的收復從未發生。燕京是遼人自己燒掉送給宋軍的：一個空城，一片焦土，和一城被驅趕的百姓。宣和四年（1122）初，幽州降卒與漢軍反噬，燕京再失，童貫南退，宋廷的攻燕成了笑柄；同年遼之燕京降於金，金人用兵據有燕雲，「海上之盟」的實際內容暴露：宋人出力破遼，金人坐收燕雲。宣和五年遼亡，七年靖康之變，河北燕山一線自此淪入金國之手，直到宋金和議之後才有部分歸還，而且往往只剩下空城與地名。北伐軍隊在幽燕所為亦難免嚴酷：拆城取材、徵用民夫、掠府庫、驅丁壯，仇恨留在當地，成為1122年變亂的根由。對遼而言，幫源洞是一場真正的勝利：宗弼以城守之兵破宋軍於野，保住了自己西撤的通道；代價是燕京自此再無完整宮室府庫，一座五京之一的都城在火中燒成焦土，遼廷的實力與民心自此再不能支。對金而言，宗弼此後歸金，以漢人將領的身分成為金國初年最能戰的主帥之一。對兵器史而言，這一役同時留下兩個燃燒的記錄：遼軍在燕京城內放的火，和宋軍攻城時用過的猛火油與火藥兵器；它們說明十二世紀的攻城與守城，最後常常不是由器械的精巧分出勝負，而是由誰能把自己的火送到對方城牆上。
impactEn: The effect of this battle was the first collapse of the Song policy of recovering You and Yun. In Tong Guan's report the court gained Yanjing, gained the rewards, and gained the formula of being brother to the Khitans with the old land restored to Song; but the real recovery never happened. Yanjing was burned by the Liao and handed to the Song army: an empty city, a stretch of scorched ground, and a population driven out of its own gates. In the early months of Xuanhe 4 (1122) the surrendered soldiers and the Han troops of Youzhou turned and bit back, Yanjing was lost a second time, and Tong Guan fell back south, and the Song's assault on Yanjing became a laughing stock. In that same year Yanjing went over to the Jin, and the Jin took You and Yun by force; the true content of the pact of the sea lay bare, that the Song had spent the effort to break the Liao and the Jin had sat still and taken the prefectures. In 1125 the Liao perished, in 1127 came the disaster of Jingkang, and the line of Hebei and Yanshan passed into the hands of the Jin, to be returned in part only after the Song-Jin peace, and then often as nothing more than an empty town and a name. The conduct of the expedition in You and Yan was harsh as well: walls pulled down for their timber, corvée for the people, the treasury stripped, the workers driven off, and the hatred left behind in the country, which became the root of the revolt of 1122. For the Liao, Aidingyuan was a real victory: Zongbi broke the Song army in the field with the troops of the garrison and kept open the road by which they withdrew; the price was that Yanjing never again possessed intact palaces or treasury, and one of the five capitals of the empire was burned down to a shell, from which neither the strength nor the confidence of the Liao court could rise again. For the Jin, Zonghib entered their service and became one of the most formidable commanders of the early Jin, a Han general leading their banners. For the history of weapons this campaign left two records of burning at once: the fire the Liao set inside the city of Yanjing, and the burning oil and gunpowder weapons the Song used in the assault. They show that in the twelfth century the taking and the holding of a walled city was decided less often by the refinement of the engines than by the question of who could carry his own fire to the foot of the enemy's wall.
result: 結果是遼軍的戰術勝利，宋軍的紙面勝利。宗弼在幫源洞擊破宋軍先鋒，追至燕京城下，蕭綽與他議定焚城而去，遂將府庫珍貨、人口牲畜搜刮一空，四面縱火，然後率眾撤出，留下一座燃燒的燕京給宋軍。童貫的中路大軍抵達時只見煙火與空郭，遂奏「克燕」；宋軍入城，封府庫、收圖籍、括物資，與論功行賞，一時視為宣和以來第一大功，蔡攸、王黼、童貫一併加賞，童貫進封廣陽郡王、拜太師，劉延慶、蔡靖等各論功行。真正的敗局在第二年顯形：幽州漢軍反，張覺叛，燕京復陷於遼之殘部與叛軍之手，童貫引軍南還，張覺為遼人所誅；遼主天祚帝西走，終為金人所擒，遼國在宣和五年（1125）亡。燕雲十六州終未歸宋，宣和七年（1127）靖康之變起，北宋覆亡。就本卡兵器而言，這場戰爭沒有希臘火參與，但也因此格外清楚地標出了一條界線：真正在燕京燃燒的是遼軍的退城火與宋軍的猛火油，而同一年希臘火仍在敘利亞的城塞前發威；燃燒兵器在十二世紀仍是攻城的最後手段，其威力不在配方，而在於誰能把火送到城牆之下。
resultEn: The result was a tactical victory for the Liao and a paper victory for the Song. Zongbi broke the Song vanguard at Aidingyuan and pursued to the walls of Yanjing; the Empress Dowager and he agreed to burn the city and go, and so they stripped the treasury of its treasure and drove off the people and the cattle, set fire on all four sides, and withdrew with their men, leaving a burning Yanjing to the Song army. When Tong Guan's central army arrived it saw only smoke and a hollow town and reported the capture of Yanjing; the Song entered the city, sealed the treasury, gathered the archives, took stock of the goods, and the court divided honours, for a time treating it as the greatest success since the beginning of Xuanhe. Cai Yao, Wang Fu and Tong Guan were rewarded together, Tong Guan was advanced to Prince of Guangyang and Grand Preceptor, and Liu Yanqing, Cai Jing and the rest were each rewarded for their part. The real disaster showed itself in the following year: the Han troops of Youzhou rose, Zhang Jue rebelled, Yanjing fell again into the hands of the Liao remnants and the rebels, Tong Guan led his army south, and Zhang Jue was executed by the Liao. The Liao emperor Tianzuo fled west and was at last taken by the Jin, and the Liao state perished in 1125. The sixteen prefectures of You and Yun never came to the Song; in 1127 the disaster of Jingkang came and the Northern Song perished. As for the weapon on this card, Greek fire took no part in this war, and for that very reason the campaign marks a boundary with unusual clarity: what actually burned at Yanjing was the fire of the Liao in their burning city and the burning oil of the Song at the walls, while in the same year Greek fire was still roaring before the fortresses of Syria. In the twelfth century the burning weapon remained the last resort of the siege, and its power lay not in the formula but in who could carry the fire to the foot of the wall.
